description: Machine-readable usage contracts for the iosense application chrome. Each guard states what the component is for, how an AI should choose its props, which combinations are illegal, and the anti-patterns that keep recurring.
readFirst: IosenseShell.guard.json — it is the entry point, and mounting the pieces without it is the single most common way to get a shell that looks nearly right. Then AppSideNav.guard.json, whose three-state model (pinned / peeked / collapsed) is the thing most likely to be got wrong.
invariants: This package is NOT dependency-free. It is built on @faclon-labs/design-sdk and @faclon-labs/fds and inherits their tokens. Use @faclon-labs/app-shell if you need a portable shell.

IosenseShell is the entry point. The individual components do NOT render the markup the content-area CSS targets (data-topbar, data-sidenav-pinned, .app-scroll-frame, .app-main-scroll), so assembling them by hand loses the content inset, the overlay scrollbar and the rail offset.

The rail ships EMPTY and NO SAMPLE NAV IS EXPORTED. The rows we built are the iosense product pages and were only ever demo content; they live in demo/iosenseNav.tsx, alongside the sample profile and notifications in demo/sampleData.ts. Copy them; you cannot import them.
Set the logo prop. Left unset, design-sdk falls through to its own built-in iosense mark, so an unbranded install silently ships our identity.

A nav row has a FIXED shape and the host supplies only two things: the glyph and the label text. Icon 14px square (clamped in CSS, so a stray size={64} is harmless), label one ellipsised line (never wraps), 14px/400 type, 32px row. Section labels 12px. The active row keeps weight 400. None of it is a host decision.
The rail footer ships EMPTY. Help is what the iosense product puts there; it is not chrome. Build footer rows with NavFooterRow so labels fade with the rail.

buildTrail reads the SAME navItems array the rail renders, so the trail and the rail cannot disagree about the hierarchy. Only accordions become breadcrumb ancestors — a section groups rows visually and is never an ancestor.

Three stylesheets, in order: @faclon-labs/design-sdk/styles.css, then @faclon-labs/fds/styles.css, then theme-overrides.css. The SDK sheet is REQUIRED — it is the only definition of --spacing-*, and without it the content sheet's padding-inline is invalid and silently collapses to 0.
theme-overrides.css must be imported AFTER the SDK stylesheets AND after the component imports. design-sdk injects component CSS when its modules load, so overrides imported earlier lose the cascade.

The content container is padded 16px left, right and TOP, and NOT at the bottom — it is the scroll container and a scrolling column has no bottom to pad. Blocks inside it are 16px apart by default. One owner: .app-main-scroll. Page roots add nothing, and children go in with no wrapper, no padding and no margin.
The rail has THREE states, not two: pinned (a click, moves the page), peeked (a hover, floats over it) and collapsed. Never key behaviour on isPinned to mean "open".
The hover peek is owned in React, not by the SDK. Both state objects strip the SDK data-hovered attribute, because React cannot see it and the component has to know it is expanded.
The collapse control lives in the top bar, never in the rail: a control that hides a panel cannot sit inside it.
A breadcrumb crumb with no href is inert text. Sections that are not pages are exactly that case.
Tooltips appear only when a label is unreadable — the 48px strip, or a truncated expanded label. Never when the text is legible.
The application launcher and the assistant button are deliberately not exported. AppTopBar takes an actions slot instead.
Never put a ref on the direct child of an fds Tooltip or Popover — the clone spreads children.props after ref and the component silently never opens.

The package exports CHROME ONLY. It does not carry helpers for the app pages the chrome navigates to — the profile form options, the avatar upload helpers, the notification date formatters and the language picker were all removed, because no component here used any of them and exporting them implied this package would help build screens it knows nothing about.

The top bar is three regions and nothing else: the rail toggle and the breadcrumbs on the left, then the actions slot, the notifications bell and the avatar on the right, in that fixed order. There is no search, title or tab slot — anything else a product wants goes through actions, to the LEFT of the bell and avatar so it cannot displace them.

CONTENT RENDERED INTO THE MAIN CONTAINER COMES FROM THE SDK. Cards, tables, charts, buttons, inputs, badges, empty states and modals all exist in @faclon-labs/design-sdk and @faclon-labs/fds; a div styled to look like one will not follow the theme, will not match the next page, and will drift when the real component changes. LAYOUT is the exception — arranging those components is the page author job, because the SDK ships no layout primitive for it.

The content container pads 16px left, right and top EQUALLY. Every direct child gets the 16px gap even when it draws nothing, so an svg defs block or a portal anchor placed inside pushes the first visible block to 32px from the top while the sides stay 16 — keep invisible helpers outside the shell.
